english: A rectangle $R$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes is inscribed in the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$. Its vertex $V(x,y)$ in the first quadrant moves on the circle so that $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-1$ unit per second. Using differentials, the approximate area of $R$ (in square units) $0.1$ second after the instant at which $V$ is at $(3,4)$ is
hindi: निर्देशांक अक्षों के समान्तर भुजाओं वाला एक आयत $R$ वृत्त $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ के अन्तर्गत है। प्रथम चतुर्थांश में इसका शीर्ष $V(x,y)$ वृत्त पर इस प्रकार गति करता है कि $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-1$ इकाई प्रति सेकण्ड। अवकलों का उपयोग करके, जिस क्षण $V$ बिन्दु $(3,4)$ पर है उससे $0.1$ सेकण्ड बाद $R$ का सन्निकट क्षेत्रफल (वर्ग इकाई में) है
solution_full: The rectangle has vertices $(\pm x,\pm y)$, so its sides are $2x$ and $2y$ and its area is $A=4xy$. At $V(3,4)$, $A=4\cdot 3\cdot 4=48$.
Since $V$ stays on the circle, $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ for all $t$. Differentiating with respect to $t$: $2x\dfrac{dx}{dt}+2y\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$.
At $(3,4)$ with $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-1$: $3(-1)+4\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dt}=\dfrac{3}{4}$ (the vertex rises as it moves left, as it must on the circle).
By the product rule, $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=4\left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\,y+x\,\dfrac{dy}{dt}\right)=4\left((-1)(4)+3\cdot\dfrac{3}{4}\right)=4\left(-4+\dfrac{9}{4}\right)=-7$ square units per second.
Treating $A$ as a function of $t$, the differential gives $\Delta A\approx dA=\dfrac{dA}{dt}\,\Delta t$ with $\Delta t=0.1$: $\Delta A\approx -0.7$.
Hence the approximate area after $0.1$ second is $48-0.7=47.3$ square units.
(For comparison, the exact area is about $47.25$, so the approximation is sound.)
originality_note: New: a related-rate of the area of a rectangle whose vertex slides on a circle, fed into a differential (linear-in-time) estimate (way 5). Closest known: rate of change of area of an inscribed rectangle. Different because: the rate is not the answer; it is used through dA = A'(t) dt to estimate a later area, so both concepts are needed.

concept_use.Rate measure and related rates: dy/dt from x^2+y^2=25 and dA/dt = 4(x y' + y x') = -7 at (3,4).
concept_use.Approximation and errors using different: Delta A ~ (dA/dt) Delta t gives the approximate area 48 - 0.7 = 47.3.
